newsitem.title: USA: Clinton plan for city appears unacceptable - Norton.
newsitem.headline: Clinton plan for city appears unacceptable - Norton.

text.p: D.C.'s delegate to the U.S. Congress expressed disappointment on Wednesday that President Clinton's upcoming fiscal 1998 budget plan apparently will not call for a flat tax for the financially struggling city.
Clinton said in his State of the Union address on February 4 that his budget, due out on February 6, will take an empowerment zone "approach" to solving D.C.'s massive financial problems.
He said the plan would include "private sector tax incentives" to renew the D.C. "so that Washington is a great place to work and live and, once again, the proud face America shows the world."
But Norton said in a press statement on February 5 that the President's plan is "unacceptable" if it also does not do more to stop massive taxpayer flight from the city.
Norton, a Democrat, wants the President to back a proposed 15 percent flat tax for city residents. She introduced flat tax legislation earlier this week.
